chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Yas'a from his father who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot the Qunut in the obligatory prayer; he said, 'There is no re-performance (making up the prayer) upon him.'
And what has been narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said: I asked him about a man who forgets the Qunut until he bows; should he perform Qunut? He said, 'No.'

So it is permissible that the Imam (peace be upon him) meant that re-performance is not obligatory upon him, because the Qunut's original status is not obligatory; so how can its re-performance be obligatory?
And it is merely a recommended, sunnah practice; thus its re-performance is also merely recommended and sunnah, rather than being obligatory.
And it is permissible that the Imam (peace be upon him) meant there is no re-performance upon him if the state is one of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah).
That which clarifies and explains this is what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the Qunut during the obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of Qunut in obligatory prayers, establishing that its non-obligatory status means forgetting it does not necessitate re-performing the prayer (i'adah). The text provides a nuanced scholarly analysis, suggesting the Imam’s ruling may reflect either the inherent recommended nature of Qunut or the context of taqiyyah (dissimulation), thereby distinguishing between wajib and mustahabb acts in ritual jurisprudence. This highlights the Shia method of deriving legal subtleties from concise prophetic statements by examining underlying causes and historical contexts.
